about: Prisma's milestone checkpoints (Port/docs/ROADMAP.md). The MILESTONES page in Prisma reads and updates this file; commit it to share progress.

milestones.M1: Gameplay parity: playing Cosmic Shore in Prisma is indistinguishable from the Unity build.
milestones.M2: Unity-free development: developers stop opening Unity; Prisma's own tools do every Unity job Cosmic Shore needs.

checkpoints.title: Online parity
checkpoints.exit: An `INetTransport` seam with TCP as its first transport (can start before G2); then 4 players over the internet in each multiplayer mode; Steam auth and achievements; cloud save and leaderboards on the chosen backend
notes: 2026-10-08 status -> in-progress (Prisma)

2026-10-08 Pre-G2 part done: INetTransport/INetTransportFactory seam (src/CosmicShore.Engine/Networking/Wire/INetTransport.cs). NetSocket is the TCP implementation; NetDriver opens transports only through NetDriver.TransportFactory (default TcpTransportFactory); wire protocol unchanged. Tests: NetTransportContractTests (7 checks x {tcp, loopback}), NetDriverTransportTests (7, the handshake over the loopback and over real TCP), NetWireTests; `dotnet test` on those = Passed 24/24, 4 runs. engine_build player = ok, 0 warnings, right after the change; engine_smoke (build:false) = PASS, Bootstrap -> Authentication, 0 errors; unity_isolation_check = ok. The full engine_test and a fresh player build could not run at the end: other sessions' in-flight edits in this worktree (tests/ParityDiffTests.cs, Audio/Fmod.cs) do not compile. Not done: a two-process LAN Bloomrush regression run (no scripted harness). Exit criterion NOT met: internet relay, Steam auth/achievements, cloud save and leaderboards wait for gate G2 (2026-12-15); the post-G2 work is on the board.

2026-10-08 Multiplayer test tools (docs/MULTIPLAYER.md, steps 0-4): --realtime headless pacing, NetSimulator (latency/jitter/loss/bandwidth/cable pull over any INetTransport), NetStats (per-peer traffic, kinds, RPCs, RTT; do net; window title; session report), NetFaults (session-service full/ratelimit/relayfail/down/slow), the Launcher NET page and MCP net_* tools (MultiplayerRun). Evidence: CosmicShore.Tests 1824/1824 at step 3, plus SimulatedTransportTests 14, NetStatsTests 8, NetFaultsTests 10, MultiplayerRunTests 7; two real headless players: localhost RTT 27.7 ms, +200 ms under netsim latency=100 on one side, netfault full refused a join with the game's own message, a 10 s cable pull dropped the guest on both ends. Exit criterion still NOT met: internet relay, Steam, cloud save and leaderboards wait for G2; the reliable-UDP transport (step 5) is next.

2026-10-08 Step 5 (docs/MULTIPLAYER.md §6.6): Froglet's UDP transport (UdpTransport: reliable-ordered fragments, selective acks, RTT-timed resends with a 30 ms floor, token handshake, keepalive, 10 s timeout, flush-on-close) plus an unreliable channel used only by NetworkTransforms whose prefab sets UseUnreliableDeltas (stamped poses, stale-drop, reliable teleports and settle keyframes). Now the default transport for networked players (COSMIC_SHORE_NET_TRANSPORT=tcp keeps TCP). Evidence: CosmicShore.Tests 1867/1867; contract checks over udp and sim-udp; frames whole and in order under 10% and 30% real datagram loss; the five-player party harness 14/14 on UDP, and 13/14 with every player on a simulated 4G line (the failure was game defect B29, fixed separately in Assets).

2026-10-09 Step 6 (docs/MULTIPLAYER.md §6.7): the relay. IDatagramLink under UdpTransport (DirectLink = a socket, RelayLink = Unity Relay's message protocol: HMAC-signed BIND, CONNECT_REQUEST/ACCEPTED, RELAY, PING keep-alive, re-bind on mismatch/timeout, CLOSE), a client for the Relay Allocations REST API, and FrogletRelayServer (CosmicShore --relay-server) speaking the same protocol and REST shape. The session service allocates before StartHost and records a join code; a joiner joins by code. Switches: COSMIC_SHORE_RELAY, NET page Connection = RELAY, net_players relay=local, net_scenario relay=true, PRISMA_RELAY=1. Evidence: RelayTests 10/10 (BIND HMAC against a Python reference), contract checks over relay and sim-relay, MultiplayerRunTests 16/16, Launcher tests 21/21, CosmicShore.Tests 1891/1891; the five-player party harness 14/14 with every pilot through the relay (22 allocations, 21,227 datagrams forwarded, 0 refused). Exit criterion still NOT met: UGS's own relay needs sign-in (P7, Docs/MULTIPLAYER_START_HERE.md), and nothing has run across two real networks yet.

checkpoints.title: Performance parity
checkpoints.exit: On the GTX 1060: every mode at every intensity within 10% of Unity's frame time, and load times within the R7 target. Includes GPU timer queries in the session report, the `tasks` phase's allocations (279-728 KB/frame in Menu_Main, steady GC up to 1.9 ms/frame), jobs moved to `Parallel.For` only where a profile shows them, and a `SustainedLowLatency` A/B
notes: 2026-10-08 status -> in-progress (Prisma)
2026-10-08 run stopped at the 80-turn limit; what it tried is board item T-6 (Prisma)

2026-10-08 Measured headless Menu_Main (1500 frames, --session-report): the `tasks` phase allocates 0 KB/frame now (the 279-728 KB figure is gone); the cost was the trigger pass - 256 pooled SpawnablePrism trigger boxes parked at the origin, no Rigidbody, 32,640 pairs and their OnTriggerStay every step (trig.pairs 9.6 ms, trig.stays 11.4 ms; new trig.exits/enters/stays/contacts markers). With the Rigidbody rule: fixed phase 24.9 -> 0.55 ms avg, sim p95 100 -> 4 ms, fixed-phase allocations 113.6 -> 0.2 KB/frame, steady GC pause 0.13 -> 0.02 ms/frame. engine_smoke MinigameJoust_Gameplay 512 s -> 15 s for 900 frames. Pre-existing smoke failures (unchanged by the rule): Freestyle and AstroLeague were engine gaps, fixed the same day (Container.InjectGameObject walks a snapshot; AddComponent<ParticleSystem> adds its ParticleSystemRenderer) and both smoke PASS; Joust entered directly still NREs in ThemeManagerDataContainerSO.GetTeamTransparentBlockMaterial (TeamMaterialSets is filled by Bootstrap's ThemeManager) - a play-from-scene assumption of the game, not an engine gap. Not yet done for C7: GTX 1060 frame times against Unity, load times, GPU timer comparison, SustainedLowLatency A/B.

2026-10-08 Instruments landed: session reports now carry scenes[].loadMs (scene switch to its first presented frame) and bootMs (process start to first frame), memory.gcLatencyMode, and the player takes --gc-latency low (SustainedLowLatency). Prisma TIME benchmarks show LOAD and GPU (timer queries, WINDOW runs) with deltas against the previous run, and GC A/B runs each item in both modes. First reading (headless MinigameSkimRace entered directly, 600 frames, this container): load 10.5 s default vs 9.8 s low-latency, boot 13.1 vs 12.0 s - almost all of it first-use JIT and content; idle frames under 0.1 ms in both. Left for C7: the same on the GTX 1060 in WINDOW mode against Unity (Y4 on the user's machine), and a replay-driven A/B with play in it.
